headline: Hawaiian integration is done and loyalty is growing fast, but a guided full-year loss and 8.8x leverage leave little margin for error.
business: Alaska Air Group combines Alaska Airlines (Seattle, Portland, Bay Area, Los Angeles) with Hawaiian Airlines (acquired 2024), adding widebodies for Pacific and new Seattle long-haul flying. A oneworld member with a strong West Coast loyalty base.
recent: Q3 2026 revenue $4.3B (+14%), unit revenue up nearly 12% on capacity +2.4%; GAAP net loss $147M ($1.32/share).
Adjusted EPS $0.36 excluding a $0.67 tax catch-up ($0.31 loss including it); full-year 2026 guided to an adjusted loss of $5.00-$5.50/share on a $1.8B fuel headwind.
Loyalty cash remuneration +21% to $721M and managed corporate revenue +30%; the single passenger service system went live in Q2.
strengths: Low price/book (1.2x) and 35% upside to target
risks: Net debt/EBITDA of 8.8x and a guided 2026 loss
Most expensive EV/EBITDA of the network carriers (15.9x)
catalysts: Liquidity rebuild and debt paydown once fuel stabilizes
